3. Summary of Effects
A. Long-Term Beneficial Effects 
1. Provision of rail passenger service would increase ease of accessibility to the Central Business District (CBD) and all points along the transit route, particularly for the transit dependent. Mobility would be improved for the elderly and handicapped.
2. The project should stimulate the regional economy and spur development, especially in the Buffalo-Amherst Corridor.
3. The mall and associated reduction in auto travel would enhance the pedestrian and transportation environment in the Central Business District.
4. The project would allow local planners to adopt policies which could reduce automobile use, thereby promoting energy savings and improved regional air quality.
B. Long-Term Adverse Effects
1. Approximately twenty-one parcels, twelve privately owned, would be taken along Main Street. Eight structures would be razed.
2. If the South Yard site is selected for the service and storage facility, 2.1 acres of vacant public land and 7.7 acres of private land would be taken; twenty-two structures would be razed. If the Ellicott Yard site is chosen, 3.4 acres of vacant public land and 13.7 acres of private land would be taken; two large ware-houses would be razed. If the Terminal Yard site is selected and a new spur constructed to maintain rail service to businesses across South Park Avenue from the yard, 8.3 acres of public land (encompassing the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad depot property) and 2.6 acres of private land would be taken; three structures would be razed.
3. Mixed-traffic operations may result in increased accidents. However, the trend in numbers of accidents is not certain; the anticipated reduction in vehicular traffic in this section may result in a better rather than worse safety record.
